cards.prose: Leviticus 22 is where Moses' word about the holy things is found, and it is spoken to Aaron and his sons, the priests, about who may eat of what the people hallow. Nothing in it tells every man to wash before he eats bread. The Pharisees took a rule for the priests and laid it on every table as *the tradition of the elders*.
cards.member_sentence: The word Yahuah (the LORD) spoke to Moses about the holy things was for Aaron and his sons, not for every man's table.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is not making up a charge. He reads the Pharisees Isaiah's own verse, where *this people* draw near with mouth and lips and their fear of Yahuah (the LORD) is *taught by the precept of men*. Mark's wording and Isaiah's say one thing: the lips are near and *their heart is far from me*.
cards.member_phrase: their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the people honoured Yahuah (the LORD) with mouth and lips while their fear of him had become something men taught them.

cards.prose: Moses shut this door before any elder tried to open it. *Ye shall not add unto the word*, he said, and the washing of *pots and cups* is a thing added beside the commandment and held as if it weighed the same. Yahusha (Jesus) is holding them to what Moses wrote.
cards.member_sentence: Moses forbids adding to or taking from the commandments, the rule the washing of pots and cups breaks.

cards.prose: Moses says it a second time, right after warning Yashar'el (Israel) not to copy how the nations served their gods: *thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it*. Said twice, so that no elder could claim he was only helping. The washing of pots and cups is something added, and Yahusha (Jesus) names it for what it is, the tradition of men.
cards.member_sentence: Moses repeats that nothing is to be added to or taken from what Yahuah (the LORD) commanded.

cards.prose: The commandment he has in mind is one of the Ten: *Honour thy father and thy mother*. A few verses on he shows how they rejected it. A man says Corban, it is a gift, and he is free from helping his parents. The tradition got kept and the fifth commandment did not, which is what rejecting *the commandment of Elohim (God)* looks like here.
cards.member_sentence: Honour thy father and thy mother is the commandment the Corban saying set aside.

cards.prose: Moses gives the same commandment again to the next generation and adds a reason, *that it may go well with thee*. The honour is meant to keep being done in house after house. The Corban saying, where a son calls what would have helped his parents a gift and so is free of it, stops it at the door of the very house it was given to.
cards.member_sentence: Moses repeats honour of father and mother as the commandment Yahuah (the LORD) gave, with a promise that it may go well.

cards.prose: John says it plainly: *if we keep his commandments* is how we know that we know him. The Pharisees were keeping their own tradition and rejecting the commandment of Elohim (God), and John's next verse speaks of exactly such a man: *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.* (1 John 2:4)
cards.member_sentence: John makes keeping his commandments the way we know we know him, the test the Pharisees' tradition fails.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) turns from the Pharisees to the whole crowd and asks every one of them to hearken, because he is about to say where defilement lives. Jeremiah had already said what the heart is, *deceitful above all things*, and the next verse says who can see into it: *I Yahuah (LORD) search the heart, I try the reins* (Jeremiah 17:10).
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah says the heart is deceitful above all things, which is where Yahusha (Jesus) says what defiles a man comes from.

cards.prose: The cure for a heart like that is not found in a washing bowl. Moses says Yahuah (the LORD) himself *will circumcise thine heart*, in the same passage where he promises to gather the ones driven out to the outmost parts of heaven. The mending of the heart is in the Torah from Moses on.
cards.member_phrase: will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed
cards.member_sentence: Moses promises that Yahuah (the LORD) himself will circumcise the heart, the cure the Torah already holds for a defiled heart.

cards.prose:
Yahusha (Jesus) is speaking about the belly: what a man eats goes *into the belly, and goeth out into the draught*, and never reaches the heart, where he says defilement is made. Which beasts a man may eat is a different question, and Moses had answered it:

*These are the beasts which ye shall eat among all the beasts that are on the earth.* (Leviticus 11:2)
cards.member_sentence: Leviticus 11 is where Yahuah (the LORD) told Moses and Aaron which beasts Yashar'el (Israel) may eat, a question Mark's sentence about the belly does not answer.

cards.prose: The disciples who asked him about this saying heard a word about the belly, and Peter, one of them, is still saying years later, *I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean*. He says it after the resurrection. What he had kept all his life he is still keeping, which is how he understood what Yahusha (Jesus) said at that table.
cards.member_sentence: Peter, years after the resurrection, still says he has never eaten anything common or unclean, so the list Moses gave still stood for the apostles.

cards.prose:
What Yahusha (Jesus) says comes out of the heart is a walk down the commandments. *Murders* is *Thou shalt not kill*, and *adulteries* is the commandment that follows it:

*Thou shalt not commit adultery.* (Exodus 20:14)

The things that defile a man are the Ten broken, which is why he sends the crowd to the heart and not to the washing bowl.
cards.member_sentence: Thou shalt not kill is the commandment broken by the murders Yahusha (Jesus) lists among what comes out of the heart.

cards.prose: Jeremiah asks *who can know it?* and Yahusha (Jesus) answers by reading out what the heart holds: *evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders*. The heart that is *desperately wicked* is the one that brings the list out, and no basin of water reaches that.
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah calls the heart desperately wicked, the heart that produces the list Yahusha (Jesus) reads out in Mark.

cards.prose:
The heart that brings out that list is the one Ezekiel says Yahuah (the LORD) will replace: *A new heart also will I give you*. The next verse says what the new heart is for:

*And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.* (Ezekiel 36:27)

The heart is mended so that the commandments get kept.
cards.member_phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit within, the answer to the heart that brings out the list Yahusha (Jesus) read.

cards.prose: Both gospels put the trip to Tyre and Sidon straight after the argument about unwashen hands. Matthew goes on to the woman crying after him in the open. Mark adds what Matthew leaves out: he went into a house, *would have no man know it*, and could not be hid.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew sends him to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon straight from the hand-washing talk, and a woman of Canaan comes out of the same coasts.

cards.prose: Mark does not repeat the sentence Matthew keeps, but it explains the woman he is about to meet. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples he is sent *unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*, and Mark says of her only that *The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation* (Mark 7:26). Read side by side, she looks like one of those sheep, a daughter of the scattered house living as a Greek.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the answer Yahusha (Jesus) made to his disciples about her: he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: Both give her the same turn in different words. Matthew's woman says *Truth, Adonai (Lord)* and has the dogs eating from *their masters’ table*. Mark's says Yes and puts the dogs *under the table* eating the *children’s crumbs*. Mark keeps the children in her answer, the same children who were to be filled first, so she takes his order as he gave it and asks only for what falls.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew's woman says Truth and puts the dogs at their masters' table, accepting the order he gave her and asking only for the crumbs.
